title: Proving Inequality via the Mean Value Theorem
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Prove that |sin b - sin a| <= |b - a| for all real numbers a and b.

steps.title: Apply MVT to f(x) = sin(x) on [a, b]
steps.mathExpression: \frac{\sin b - \sin a}{b - a} = f'(c) = \cos c \quad \text{for some } c \in (a, b)
steps.explanation: Since sine is continuous and differentiable everywhere, MVT applies.

steps.title: Take Absolute Values and Bound Cosine
steps.mathExpression: |\sin b - \sin a| = |\cos c| \cdot |b - a| \le 1 \cdot |b - a| = |b - a|
steps.explanation: Because |cos(c)| <= 1 for all real c, the result follows immediately.
